processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Alloy 15Al (Fe-35Mn-15Al-5Cu, at.%) ingots produced by melting high-purity (>99.9 %) raw materials in a vacuum induction furnace under argon. EDS-measured composition: Fe 44.6, Mn 35.2, Al 15.0, Cu 5.2 (at.%).
Homogenized ingots hot-rolled into plates with a thickness of 4 mm.
Plates cut into 10 × 5 × 2 mm³ samples by electrical discharge machining for Vickers hardness measurements and microstructure characterizations.
Samples solution treated at 1100 °C for 10 min under argon atmosphere, followed by oil quenching. Solution-treated Vickers hardness of 15Al = 253.4 ± 2.1 HV.
Solution-treated 15Al samples aged at 625 °C for 10 h followed by water quenching; this is the terminal state of the present sample. Resulting Vickers hardness = 888.2 ± 6.6 HV.

structures.overall_structure: Fully transformed β-Mn matrix — the α matrix had almost completely transformed into β-Mn at aging temperatures of 600 °C and above, with abundant fine BCC and FCC precipitates observed within the β-Mn.

phases_present.morphology: fine particles distributed at the interfaces between the β-Mn

precipitates.distribution: at the interfaces between the β-Mn
at the interfaces between the β-Mn

interfaces.phase_evolution: α → α + FCC Cu-rich phase → α-Mn + β-Mn + BCC phase → β-Mn + BCC phase + FCC Cu-rich phase
interfaces.interface_notes: The BCC phase at the β-Mn interfaces is attributed to local enrichment of the BCC-stabilizing element Al around the β-Mn interfaces, while the Cu-rich phase forms due to the limited solubility of Cu in Fe-based alloys and the expulsion of Cu from β-Mn during precipitation and growth (b0068). The content of FCC Cu-rich phase between β-Mn interfaces decreases with increasing Al content.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Vickers hardness measured with an HVS-1000 digital microhardness tester at a load of 9.8 N for 15 s; each sample tested 5 times and the average of 5 measurements reported.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Load of 9.8 N for 15 s; each sample tested 5 times and averaged
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure hardness after different aging treatments
characterization_methods.key_findings: 15Al aged at 625 °C for 10 h gives 888.2 ± 6.6 HV; 625 °C and 650 °C series stabilize between 800 HV and 900 HV with prolonged aging.

characterization_methods.purpose: Identify phase compositions of the alloys
characterization_methods.key_findings: XRD of aged 15Al (550 °C × 1 h shown) contains α/D0₃ together with both α-Mn and β-Mn reflections, indicating α-Mn and β-Mn co-precipitated before full transformation.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: ZEISS Sigma 300 SEM operated at 5 kV
characterization_methods.purpose: Identify precipitation of secondary phases such as α-Mn and β-Mn in aged samples
characterization_methods.key_findings: SE images (Fig. 7) show that the α → β-Mn transformation of the 15Al alloy proceeds fastest at higher aging temperatures, leaving a nearly featureless transformed matrix at 625/650 °C.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: GeminiSEM 300 SEM; scanning step size 1.5 μm for low magnification and 0.05 μm for high magnification
characterization_methods.purpose: Characterize the constituent phases and microstructural evolution during aging
characterization_methods.key_findings: For the 15Al alloy, aged conditions show the α → β-Mn transformation plus late BCC and FCC precipitation (e.g. 650 °C/3 h shows sparse magenta FCC speckles with no red α).

unmapped_findings: The 15Al (Fe-35Mn-15Al-5Cu at.%) low-density steel density measured by the Archimedes method is 6.85 g·cm⁻³; the EDS-measured composition is Fe 44.6, Mn 35.2, Al 15.0, Cu 5.2 (at.%).

The 15Al alloy (Fe-35.2Mn-15.0Al-5.2Cu) achieved an ultra-high specific hardness of 141 HV·cm³/g at its peak-hardness condition (600 °C for 6 h, 965.6 HV); its peak-hardness sample also retained a fracture toughness K_IC of 8.6 MPa·m^1/2.
The peak Vickers hardness of the 15Al alloy in this study is 965.6 HV (600 °C, 6 h); the present sample (625 °C, 10 h) lies on the ~888 HV plateau of the 625 °C aging series.
